items.title: One strong writer, parallel drafts, blind juries
items.summary: Many agents help parallel and evaluative work and hurt sequential writing (a Google study measured 39-70% worse). So: one strong showrunner, parallel diverse drafts, and blind cross-family juries that rank them.

items.title: Judges rank, code gates
items.summary: Models rank and advise; code decides. About 20 of every 25 quality checks are deterministic measurements, and a model's opinion never replaces a measured gate.

items.title: Batches cost half; cached prefixes cost a tenth or less
items.summary: Message Batches cost 50% less and a cached prompt prefix is read at 0.05-0.1 times the input price: batch non-urgent research and assessment, and keep every shared prefix byte-identical so the cache hits.

items.title: GitHub's scheduler can be hours late
items.summary: GitHub's cron can start a job hours late, so an external clock (the Cloudflare Worker's scheduled trigger) starts the tick, and a concurrency group stops two ticks from overlapping.

items.title: Upload private, schedule early, always set privacy
items.summary: Every upload goes up private with a scheduled publish time at least 6 hours ahead, and the privacy status is always set explicitly: since 2 Nov 2026 YouTube makes an upload PUBLIC when the status is left out.

items.title: Every paid step is checkpointed
items.summary: Every paid step is checkpointed by its content, so a failed run resumes where it stopped and nothing is paid for twice.

items.title: Artificial Analysis: use the /free endpoints
items.summary: Artificial Analysis: the old /api/v2/data/ endpoints answer 410 since 4 Nov 2026. Use /api/v2/language/models/free and /api/v2/media/{type}/models/free with the x-api-key header (100 requests a day, attribution required).

items.title: fal: catalogue and prices by API, costs not in queue results
items.summary: fal lists models at GET /v1/models (q, category, status, sort, cursor) and prices at /v1/models/pricing (unit_price, unit). Usage and invoice events need a separate key, and queue results carry no cost, so each call's cost is estimated and capped by our own code.

items.title: Hero clips: Kling 3.0 Standard on fal
items.summary: Animated hero scenes use Kling 3.0 Standard on fal (fal-ai/kling-video/o3/standard/image-to-video) at about $0.084 per second of clip.

items.title: YouTube retention curve and engaged views
items.summary: YouTube Analytics gives the retention curve as elapsedVideoTimeRatio (100 points, one video per call, ready 48-72 hours after publishing). engagedViews counts real watching and is the outcome the learning core uses.

items.title: Impressions and click-through only in the Reporting API
items.summary: Impressions and click-through rate exist only in the Reporting API report channel_reach_basic_a1: about 48 hours late and kept for 60 days, so it is pulled every day.

items.title: YouTube quota buckets and Shorts thumbnails
items.summary: videos.insert and search.list each have their own quota bucket, and thumbnails.set works for Shorts since 3 Nov 2026.

items.title: YouTube Partner Programme thresholds
items.summary: YouTube Partner Programme: 1,000 subscribers plus 4,000 long-form watch hours until 31 Jan 2027, and 8,000 hours from 1 Feb 2027 (or 10 million, then 20 million, Shorts views in 90 days). Hours watched on Shorts do not count toward the hours.

evidence.source: Growth and money research, 9 Nov 2026 (handoff research digest; requirements ledger section D)

items.title: YouTube's AI label is for realistic content
items.summary: YouTube's altered-or-synthetic content label applies to realistic content only.

evidence.source: Growth and money research, 9 Nov 2026 (handoff research digest)

items.title: Claude Max until 10 Dec 2026, then Pro
items.summary: The owner's Claude plan is Max until 10 Dec 2026 and Pro after that: code builds through Claude Code must stay small and efficient from then on.

evidence.finding: Claude Max until 10 Dec 2026 then Pro (keep Claude Code use efficient after that)
